A1.justification: Both PDFs describe d-TreeRPO. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four reasoning tasks, self-distillation and tree-configuration ablations, and training-time measurements in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds a second model backbone, controlled comparisons, probability-error measurements, sensitivity analyses and case studies.

M1.justification: Tree rollouts, bottom-up advantages, block-aligned decoding, token-wise policy updates and scheduled self-distillation remain unchanged. The complete objectives in v1 Equation (16) and v3 Equation (19) match. v3 clarifies token-wise optimization already present in v1; its revised theoretical target does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Sudoku, Countdown, GSM8K and Math500 tasks and data sources. Dataset details move from v1 Section 4.1 to v3 Appendix C.3. Additional backbones, decoding configurations and examples remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: GDPO replaces d2-stepMerge in the main accuracy comparison and training-time comparison; these are distinct methods, not renamed entries. v3 also introduces Sparse-Tree and Sparse-Flat comparators in Table 2, substantially expanding comparisons that isolate the contribution of granular credit assignment.

E3.justification: v3 adds LLaDA-MoE-7BA1B-Instruct evaluations, training/inference comparisons with block lengths 32/64/128, controls matched at 16 completions per query, four hyperparameter sweeps, and an estimation-error diagnostic using 100 samples per task. Retained headline evaluations keep their original settings. The height analysis is now described as covering 30 batches rather than 30 training steps, without establishing that it was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test equal-budget credit assignment (Table 2), decoding robustness (Figure 3), and probability-estimation error (Table 4). Appendices D–F add broader training dynamics, self-distillation hyperparameter sensitivity and a comparative GSM8K case study. Earlier tree-height, branching, self-distillation and reverse-schedule analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports explicitly defined means and standard deviations for probability-estimation error in Table 4, using Monte Carlo estimates from 32 decoding orders per sample. Neither version reports repeated-training seeds or seed-based uncertainty for headline benchmark accuracy; the addition does not establish more training runs.

E6.justification: Shared LLaDA-8B accuracy rows and the original self-distillation ablation scores remain unchanged. v3 adds MoE results, including d-TreeRPO scores of 78.3/67.2/75.5/41.2 at 256 tokens, GDPO results replacing d2-stepMerge entries, and new control, estimation-error, sensitivity and case-study findings. These are additional or replaced results, rather than same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.3 and Appendix A bound the expected joint transition-probability ratio using a worst-case confidence gap across positions and decoding orders. v3 replaces this with a quantile-based, per-token high-probability log-ratio theorem and a new proof. Its bound concerns random path-wise probabilities, replacing the earlier joint-probability bounds and Taylor expansion.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline LLaDA-8B gains remain the same. v3 expands the introduction's claimed empirical generality to two backbones and reframes the theoretical contribution around prediction probabilities rather than joint parent-to-child transition probabilities.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning unverifiable objectives and zero-shot/pass@1 coverage, plus a reported Dream output-format failure. It interprets matched-budget controls as evidence for granular credit assignment and adds hyperparameter failure explanations in Appendix E. v1's explanation of generation-length sensitivity is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact prompt templates and task-specific reward definitions, discloses rollout temperature 0.9 and gamma 2, and supplies code and checkpoint links. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying retained experiments. Dataset links are relocated; Algorithm 1 and the previous SAPO reimplementation marker are removed.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands descriptions of six baselines and their distinctions in credit assignment and probability estimation. Related-work coverage adds GDPO, BGPO, block diffusion and other works, while removing the SDAR citation. The revision goes beyond bibliographic updates and develops the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and method explanations are extensively rewritten and condensed. v3 removes the experimental research-question list and separate algorithm-summary subsection, integrates the complete objective into Section 3.4, and adds a limitations section and organized supplementary sections. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged into a 2×2 grid, Table 1 gains a second backbone block, and the runtime table is transposed. Numerous diagnostic, sensitivity and case-study displays are added; retained figures are reformatted and relocated, and the algorithm display is removed.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget controls and probability-error diagnostic address important weaknesses in v1's evidence for its proposed mechanisms. A second backbone, sensitivity analyses, and explicit prompts and rewards substantially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. Removing d2-stepMerge reduces comparison coverage, and the replacement theorem has a different target rather than a stronger expected-probability guarantee. Nevertheless, the added controls and documentation provide substantial overall gains.
